VulcanForms announces $500M financing agreement
VulcanForms plans to build three factories by the end of 2027, fueled by a $500 million financing deal the company announced Thursday. Photo I Courtesy VulcanForms
By Paula J. Owen
November 13, 2026
Share
Copy URL
Email
Facebook

Linkedin
VulcanForms plans to build three factories by the end of 2027 including one in Massachusetts, fueled by a $500 million financing deal the company announced Thursday.
“Factory No. 4” is planned for Massachusetts, according to VulcanForms CEO Kevin Kassekert, who confirmed the company also plans to double its workforce to approximately 1,000 by the end of 2027.
The financing, led by J.P. Morgan and Apollo-managed funds, supports three additional factories by the metal parts manufacturer that has existing operations in Newburyport and two in Devens where it is adding 1 million square-feet of manufacturing space .
VulcanForms, a pioneer in advanced digital manufacturing, said it plans to use the funding to accelerate the next phase of American industrial production.
Backed by multibillion-dollar commercial programs across critical industries, VulcanForms said it is expanding to meet growing customer demand, marking a milestone in the company’s transition from breakthrough manufacturing technology to industrial-scale production, according to a press release.
ADVERTISEMENT
As American industries seek to strengthen domestic production and reduce dependence on fragmented global supply chains, the challenge extends beyond technological innovation to manufacturing complex, high-performance components at the scale, speed and cost required to compete globally, the company said.
VulcanForms is addressing the challenge through a fully integrated digital manufacturing platform that combines metal additive manufacturing, precision machining, automation and physical AI.
By unifying traditionally fragmented production processes, the company is establishing a new model for producing critical components competitively in the U.S., it says.
Kevin Kassekert, CEO of VulcanForms Photo I Courtesy VulcanForms
“America cannot lead the next industrial revolution if we can’t manufacture what we invent,” Kassekert said. “For too long, breakthrough technologies developed here have been manufactured overseas.
ADVERTISEMENT
“VulcanForms is proving we can change that by turning American innovation into industrial-scale production and demonstrating that the U.S. can not only compete, but also win on the global stage. We’re proud to work with J.P. Morgan and Apollo on helping to build America’s industrial future at home.”
VulcanForms uses advanced 3D printing and machining to make complex metal parts for industries like aerospace, medical and defense. The company has presented itself as part of an effort to reshore manufacturing and to secure domestic supply chains.
The firm was awarded $21.26 million in tax credits from the Massachusetts Economic Assistance Coordinating Council to support the construction of a 1-million-square-foot advanced manufacturing facility in Devens.
The expansion is part of an effort to establish a multi-facility VulcanForms campus in Devens, according to ConnectCRE.com .

VulcanForms: $500 Million Financing Led By J.P. Morgan And Apollo To Build Three New U.S. Manufacturing Factories
By Amit Chowdhry
Nov 14, 2026
VulcanForms: $500 Million Financing Led By J.P. Morgan And Apollo To Build Three New U.S. Manufacturing Factories
VulcanForms, a Boston-based advanced digital manufacturing company, has secured an agreement for $500 million in financing led by J.P. Morgan and funds managed by Apollo. The financing will support construction of three new factories, expansion of domestic production capacity, and further development of the company’s integrated manufacturing platform as it responds to demand from customers across aerospace, defense, medical devices, consumer products, and industrial markets.
The transaction will help VulcanForms expand beyond its three existing manufacturing sites, bringing its planned manufacturing footprint to six facilities.
The company has secured multibillion-dollar commercial programs spanning several industries that require complex, high-performance metal components.
VulcanForms combines metal additive manufacturing, precision machining, automation, and physical AI within a unified production system designed to manufacture engineered parts at industrial scale.
The new financing is part of JPMorganChase’s Security and Resiliency Initiative, which supports investment in industries and supply chains considered important to U.S. economic security.
Building Three Additional Advanced Manufacturing Facilities
VulcanForms plans to use the financing to accelerate construction of three factories that will expand its domestic manufacturing capabilities.
The company currently operates manufacturing facilities in Devens and Newburyport, Massachusetts.
Its expansion reflects growing demand for advanced manufacturing services among customers seeking domestic production of sophisticated metal components.
These products frequently require specialized production processes, high manufacturing tolerances, and extensive quality validation.
Traditional manufacturing approaches can involve multiple suppliers responsible for different stages of production.
VulcanForms is developing an integrated alternative that combines several manufacturing processes within a coordinated digital infrastructure.
The company believes this approach can reduce production complexity, improve efficiency, and help manufacturers respond more quickly to changing customer requirements.
The additional facilities will provide capacity to support existing commercial programs and future production opportunities.
Combining Metal Additive Manufacturing And Physical AI
VulcanForms’ manufacturing platform integrates metal additive manufacturing with precision machining, automation, and AI-driven production capabilities.
Metal additive manufacturing uses digital designs to produce components through a process that builds material into a desired shape.
This approach can enable complex geometries that may be difficult to manufacture through conventional methods.
However, industrial production often requires additional processing to achieve precise dimensions, surface finishes, and performance characteristics.
VulcanForms addresses these requirements by combining additive manufacturing with precision machining and product validation.
The company also incorporates physical AI into its manufacturing infrastructure.

VICI Properties: $500 Million Unsecured Term Loan Refinances 2027 Debt And Improves Revolving Credit Facility Pricing
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 5:35 PM
VICI Properties: $500 Million Unsecured Term Loan Refinances 2027 Debt And Improves Revolving Credit Facility Pricing
VICI Properties, a real estate investment trust specializing in gaming, hospitality, entertainment, and experiential properties, has secured a new $500 million unsecured term loan through its subsidiary VICI Properties L.P. The financing will be used to partially refinance the company’s outstanding senior unsecured notes maturing in February 2027, while an accompanying amendment reduces borrowing costs under its existing $2.5 billion revolving credit facility.
The new loan matures on January 31, 2032, extending a portion of VICI’s debt maturity profile by approximately five years.
The loan initially carries an interest rate of the Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR) plus 90 basis points, based on a pricing grid tied to the subsidiary’s credit ratings.
The agreement also includes an improvement in pricing when the company’s total leverage ratio is at or below a specified threshold.
VICI drew the entire $500 million at closing and entered into swap agreements covering the full principal amount.
These arrangements establish an effective all-in fixed interest rate of approximately 5.20%.
The financing will help VICI address a meaningful portion of its February 2027 debt maturity by partially redeeming and refinancing its 5.75% senior unsecured notes.
By replacing part of the approaching maturity with longer-dated financing, VICI is seeking to improve its debt maturity schedule and maintain financial flexibility.
The transaction also diversifies the company’s available funding sources.
Alongside the term loan, VICI amended its existing $2.5 billion unsecured revolving credit facility.
The amendment lowers the applicable interest rate from SOFR plus 85 basis points to SOFR plus 80 basis points, subject to the company’s ratings-based pricing grid and leverage-related adjustments.
The revolving facility’s borrowing capacity and maturity remain unchanged.
These changes provide VICI with improved pricing on a significant source of corporate liquidity.
Wells Fargo Securities served as sole bookrunner for the term loan, while Wells Fargo Bank acted as administrative agent.
Wells Fargo Securities, Mizuho Bank, Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation, and Truist Securities served as joint lead arrangers.
Additional participating financial institutions included Bank of America, JPMorgan Chase Bank, Capital One, Citizens Bank, Scotiabank, Barclays, Citibank, Goldman Sachs Bank USA, and Texas Capital Bank.
VICI Properties maintains one of the largest portfolios of experiential real estate assets in North America.
The company’s holdings include 103 experiential properties, comprising 63 gaming properties and 40 other experiential assets across the United States and Canada.
Its portfolio encompasses approximately 130 million square feet and includes more than 67,000 hotel rooms and over 700 restaurants, bars, nightclubs, and sportsbooks.
Major holdings include Caesars Palace Las Vegas, MGM Grand, and the Venetian Resort Las Vegas.
The company leases its properties to gaming, hospitality, and entertainment operators under long-term triple-net lease agreements.

The new funding round will fuel Genesis' efforts to transform the range and complexity of tasks physical AI can handle, paving the way for broad adoption of Eno, the company's flagship robot
PARIS and SAN CARLOS, Calif. , Nov. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Genesis AI , a global robotics company, today announced it has raised $500 million in Series A funding at a $3.5 billion post-money valuation. The round was co-led by Premji Invest , Khosla Ventures and Eclipse , with participation from Durable Capital Partners , T. Rowe Price Associates, Inc. ¹, Bpifrance , HSG , NVIDIA , AMD Ventures , Zoom , Samsung Next and Ericsson , as well as visionary leaders including former Google CEO Eric Schmidt , Zoom CEO Eric Yuan , Jerry Yang, former CEO of Yahoo!, French tech entrepreneur Xavier Niel , and former Tesla CFO Zach Kirkhorn .
Continue Reading
Genesis AI co-founders Zhou Xian and Théophile Gervet announce the company's $500M Series A
"Our mission is to remove the physical limits on human ambition," said Zhou Xian , Co-Founder and CEO of Genesis AI. "To accomplish this, we're working to build the world's best general-purpose robot, one that works reliably in the real world, day after day. That requires the intelligence, hardware, and everything that goes into training and testing the robots to work as one system. By building it all ourselves, we can obsess over every detail and improve the entire robot faster in one closed loop. This funding will accelerate our efforts to deploy our robots in the real world at scale."
The funds will fuel the company's next phase of growth, with a focus on:
Expanding data acquisition and large-scale training to vastly extend the range and complexity of tasks robots can perform
Solving human-level physical manipulation in robots across a full range of environments and use cases, unlocking true physical AI
Deploying Eno , the company's AI-powered general-purpose robot, at scale with customers
Hiring additional world-class AI researchers, robotics experts and engineers to build the next generation of general-purpose robots
Advancing from Development to Deployment
"What stood out to us was watching Genesis robots complete long, multi-step tasks on their own at the same speed a person would, with smooth and natural movement," said Vedant Agrawal , Partner at Premji Invest. "Completing full tasks in real time, not just short clips, is what turns a robot into something a business can rely on."
"General-purpose robotics has the potential to fundamentally transform how we live and work, and Genesis is helping shape that future," said Eric Schmidt , former CEO of Google and Genesis investor. "I've believed in this team's vision since the beginning, and what they've accomplished in such a short time is extraordinary. This funding marks an important milestone as Genesis moves closer to bringing robots with human-level capabilities into the real world at scale."
Genesis is currently ramping up production of Eno, which the company is initially focused on rolling out in industrial environments including manufacturing, logistics and laboratories, before expanding into the hospitality and healthcare industries, followed by consumer and outdoor applications.

MUNICH , Nov. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Munich-based Physical AI company Agile Robots has closed a Series F funding round, raising $500 million at a valuation of $8.5 billion. The SoftBank Group-led round, with participation from NVIDIA, Hitachi Group (Hitachi and Hitachi Ventures), T.Capital and others, brings the company's total invested capital to $2 billion.
Continue Reading
Agile Robots’ $500M Series F announced on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) screens
Agile Robots builds and deploys Physical AI – humanoid and mobile robots, robotic arms and hands, and the software and AI models behind them – to help industrial customers automate tasks that have traditionally relied on human dexterity and judgment.
"Physical AI will fundamentally change how the world builds, moves and makes things," said CEO and Founder Dr. Zhaopeng Chen. "We bring Physical AI out of the lab and into industrial production, across logistics, automotive, electronics and manufacturing. This funding allows us to accelerate our global expansion, strengthen our presence in key markets and build out production capacity."
Building capacity and strengthening in strategic markets
Agile Robots plans to strengthen its presence in the United States and accelerate the development of innovative robotics applications. To expand capacity in Germany, the company opened a new production site in early 2026 at Fürstenfeldbruck, near Munich, with the capacity to produce up to 10,000 legged and wheeled humanoid robots annually.
"We believe Physical AI will transform industries. Agile Robots combines deep robotics expertise with the ability to execute at industrial scale, enabling it to bring Physical AI into everyday operations," said Dennis Chang, Managing Partner at SoftBank Investment Advisers.
Building on 20,000 deployed industrial robotic solutions
Founded in 2018 as a spin-off from the German Aerospace Center (DLR), Agile Robots has deployed 20,000 industrial robotic solutions for customers in the automotive, consumer electronics, logistics and other industries. The company has over 2,000 R&D experts and over 650 patents. Its subsidiaries include the AI robotics research platform Franka Robotics and industrial deployment specialist Krause Automation, recently acquired from thyssenkrupp AG.
About Agile Robots
Agile Robots is a leading provider of AI-powered robotics solutions to automotive, consumer electronics, healthcare and service customers. It employs more than 3,500 people from almost 60 nations. Together with its subsidiaries BÄR Automation, Franka Robotics, Idealworks and Krause Automation, it covers all areas of AI-driven robotics.

Ballistic Ventures: $490 Million Fundraising Target For Two New Cybersecurity Funds Amid AI Security Boom
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 8:51 AM
Ballistic Ventures: $490 Million Fundraising Target For Two New Cybersecurity Funds Amid AI Security Boom
Ballistic Ventures, a San Francisco-based venture capital firm specializing in cybersecurity investments, is seeking to raise $490 million across two new investment funds as artificial intelligence drives demand for technologies that protect businesses against increasingly sophisticated cyber threats. According to a TechCrunch report , the firm has filed documents with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission seeking $360 million for its third flagship fund and an additional $130 million for a separate investment vehicle called Ballistic Ventures Fund B.
The regulatory filings indicate that neither fund had recorded any capital sales at the time of submission, meaning the amounts represent fundraising targets rather than completed capital commitments.
The proposed fundraising follows Ballistic Ventures’ earlier investment vehicles, including a $300 million inaugural fund announced in 2022 and a $360 million second flagship fund raised in 2024.
The firm also previously raised approximately $130 million for a separate vehicle called Ballistic Ventures Fund A, according to PitchBook data cited by TechCrunch.
The new fundraising initiative would provide additional capital for investments in cybersecurity companies developing technologies for AI security, enterprise protection, and emerging digital threats.
Ted Schlein And Cybersecurity Industry Veterans Lead Ballistic Ventures
Ballistic Ventures was founded in late 2021 by a team of experienced cybersecurity executives and investors.
Its founding team includes Ted Schlein, a former partner at Kleiner Perkins, where he spent more than two decades investing in technology companies.
Other founders include Barmak Meftah, former President of AT&T Cybersecurity, and Roger Thornton, who co-founded cybersecurity companies Fortify Software and AlienVault.
The firm’s leadership brings experience in cybersecurity company development, enterprise software, and venture capital investing.
Ballistic Ventures focuses specifically on cybersecurity, differentiating its investment strategy from firms pursuing opportunities across multiple technology categories.
Its approach emphasizes identifying companies developing technologies designed to address evolving security challenges.
The firm has developed a portfolio spanning enterprise security, AI-related threats, and other cybersecurity applications.
Previous Investments Include Talon And Pangea
Ballistic Ventures has backed several cybersecurity companies that have subsequently been acquired by major industry participants.
Its portfolio includes Talon Cyber Security, which was acquired by Palo Alto Networks.
The firm also invested in Pangea, a security company acquired by CrowdStrike.
These transactions illustrate Ballistic Ventures’ participation in companies developing technologies attractive to established cybersecurity vendors.
Other portfolio companies include Armadin, GetReal, Nudge Security, and Oligo Security.
The businesses operate across different areas of cybersecurity, reflecting the firm’s interest in emerging security requirements.

Viasat: $450 Million U.S. Space Force Contract For Golden Dome Space Data Network Backbone Development
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 1:35 PM
Viasat: $450 Million U.S. Space Force Contract For Golden Dome Space Data Network Backbone Development
Viasat, a Carlsbad, California-based provider of satellite communications and secure networking technologies, has received an indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) contract with a ceiling of $450 million from the U.S. Space Force’s Space Systems Command (SSC). The award will support the development, deployment, sustainment, and operation of the Space Data Network Backbone (SDN-B) mission operations center, a critical component of the military’s efforts to establish resilient space-based communications infrastructure supporting Golden Dome for America and Joint Force operations.
The contract includes an initial $115 million task order to support development and scaling of the mission operations center and associated network operations capabilities.
The $450 million represents the maximum value available under the IDIQ contract rather than a guaranteed payment to Viasat. Additional work will depend on future task orders and government requirements.
The award positions Viasat as a network and mission systems integration partner supporting the Space Force’s efforts to establish a more interconnected and resilient military space architecture.
The SDN-B initiative is designed to provide high-capacity, low-latency data transport across multiple satellite networks and orbital environments.
Its architecture will support communications requirements for the U.S. Space Force, Golden Dome for America, and military operations conducted by the Joint Force worldwide.
Supporting The Golden Dome Space Data Network Backbone
The Space Data Network Backbone is a multi-vendor data transport architecture designed to connect and manage communications capabilities across participating space and ground systems.
The network is intended to provide resilient connectivity for military operations that depend on timely access to information collected and transmitted through space-based infrastructure.
Rather than relying on a single satellite operator or communications architecture, SDN-B is designed to integrate multiple providers and network elements.
This approach supports the Space Force’s broader objective of developing open architectures that can incorporate commercial technologies and adapt to changing mission requirements.
Viasat will focus on the mission operations center responsible for supporting network management and integration under government direction.
The center is intended to provide a coordinated view of participating SDN-B network elements, allowing operators to monitor connectivity, network performance, and operational status.
The infrastructure will also support government-directed prioritization of communications resources based on military mission requirements.
$115 Million Initial Task Order
The initial $115 million task order will fund work associated with establishing and scaling the SDN-B mission operations center and its network operations capabilities.
Viasat will apply its experience operating secure satellite communications networks to support the development of an enterprise-level operational infrastructure.
The company’s responsibilities include systems engineering, network integration, operational support, and sustainment activities.
